name: Hand of Dextren Ward
summary: In Darkshire, grieving families await proof that Dextren Ward has been executed in the Stormwind Stockade. His severed hand is bound for town as a sign that justice has reached him.

sections.title: A Defiler's Toll
sections.body: Lord Ebonlocke sentenced Dextren Ward to death after he caught him digging up bodies in Duskwood cemeteries. Ward sold those bodies to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Stormwind intervened before Darkshire could execute him and took him to the Stockade. For the grieving families, Ward's hand proves the defiler has been executed, despite the House of Nobles' unwanted leniency.

sections.title: A Message to the Nobles
sections.body: Councilman Millstipe's demand for Ward's severed hand defies the crown as well. Duskwood feels abandoned by Stormwind's elite, who withhold military aid yet assert their authority when it suits them. By executing a prisoner in the capital's deepest dungeon and claiming his hand, the Darkshire Council tells the House of Nobles it will enforce its own laws when the nobles fail.

faq.answer: Dextren Ward was caught unearthing corpses from Darkshire's graveyards and selling them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Duskwood sentenced him to beheading, but Stormwind authorities took him to the Stockade instead of carrying out the execution.

faq.q: Why does Darkshire want his hand?
faq.answer: Councilman Millstipe demands Ward's severed hand as proof of his execution. It brings closure to the families whose ancestors' graves were plundered and tells the House of Nobles that Darkshire's justice cannot be overridden.

faq.q: Where is the Hand of Dextren Ward found?
faq.answer: The hand is claimed directly from Dextren Ward in the deeper chambers on the left side of the Stormwind Stockade. He fights as a warrior and has a frightening shout that sends foes fleeing.

faq.q: Why did Stormwind imprison Ward instead of executing him?
faq.answer: The House of Nobles claimed jurisdiction over Ward and imprisoned him in the Stockade instead of allowing Darkshire to carry out its death sentence. Darkshire's leaders see this as corrupt interference that disregards the frontier town's plight.

angles.text: For the Alliance, Ward's imprisonment reveals the deep rift between Stormwind's distant House of Nobles and Duskwood's abandoned frontier settlers.
As a mage, you know Ward was no spellcaster. The bodies he dug up fed Morbent Fel's dark arts, so Ward's death strikes at those who traffic with the dead.
